page.layout: One printed page. Top: running head "'EMBLEMATA." with page number "115" at the upper right. Below it, a heading line "Phœnix intra flammas." with emblem number "VI." at right. Then a woodcut illustration (phoenix in flames on a rock), with no text. Below the woodcut, a block of verse in italic: a stanza of four lines with a large initial P, then a second two-line stanza. Bottom right: signature "P iiij".

l.i: Phœnicen, si Vera ferunt, mors ipsa refingit,
Huic sit Vt Vnus aui Vitaque mórsque
Ite, ô carnifices, Sanctorum sancta cremateC-
orpora, quos Vultis perdere flamma parit.

page.notes: The woodcut shows a phoenix on a rock amid flames and smoke; no printed text in the picture. The large initial "P" of the first stanza is a decorative capital; the first stanza's opening letters are set in a larger initial. The line "Hœnicen, si Vera ferunt" and the other verse words are transcribed as they appear; "Vera" and "Vt Vnus" letters for V/U in the black-letter-like forms of the scan are uncertain, and "Vitaque" and "Vultis" may read differently in the original. Some letterforms (long s, e.g. "ipsa", "Sanctorum") are rendered as plain s.
